changelog: - **CI checks, deploy scripts and bot comments no longer print a tenant name or a marketing hostname, and a forbidden-terms guard keeps such names out** (#2919). The marketing content check no longer compares the served `<title>` with a hard-coded brand. A page's `<title>` must now contain the `name` in its host's own `/manifest.webmanifest`, and that name must be neither `Internship CRM` nor the `coreCRM` fallback. The same rule runs in `scripts/marketing-content-probe.mjs` (uptime), `infra/deploy-prod.sh` and `infra/server/topic-deploy.sh` (both warn-only). The new `infra/test/marketing-title-check.test.sh` keeps the three copies in step. `uptime.yml` reads the marketing URLs from the `MARKETING_PROBE_URLS` secret and names a host only by its number. When the secret is unset it skips them with a notice and neither opens nor closes an incident about them. The deploy checks print neither the title, the manifest name nor a hostname. The deploy workflows still pass the probe host in their step script, so the deploy job log shows it until the hostnames move out of the workflow files. The topic-preview comment says "Marketing world", `android-build.yml` builds only the generic app, and `build-image.yml` no longer uploads Docker build records. New: `scripts/check-forbidden-terms.mjs` + `forbidden-terms.yml`. The guard takes its list only from the `FORBIDDEN_TERMS` secret and prints locations, never matches. It blocks a PR that adds a match (lines, file names, commit messages and authors, branch, title, body). It turns a push to `main` red when the push brings one in, which covers squash messages, fork PRs and direct pushes. Every run that has the repository's secrets fails when the list is missing. It also scans the whole tree on `main` and daily, warn-only for now.
